note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the very first render, built straight from the artist's plan.
note.changing: First build: a field of marbled paint, two slim mackerel bent along a spiral around the center with ribbons streaming from their tails, a third eye inside a flower of eye-shaped petals, and SAVES and FISH on dark banners above and below.
note.why: Ebru paper is the most liquid pattern there is, and two fish chasing tails is the oldest picture of flow.
note.idea: Two Atlantic mackerel chase each other in a circle like the Pisces sign or a yin-yang, swimming through real mathematical ebru marbling, where drops of paint are combed into patterns whose lines never cross, while a third eye opens between them.

note.saw: The marbling worked, but the fish were thin arcs that vanished at small size, their heads were flat, and the tail ribbons looked like fat seaweed noodles.
note.changing: The snouts swing out to the left and right so the two fish eyes and the third eye line up as one three-eyed face, and a honeycomb tunnel with an eye in every cell opens behind the third eye. Each fish gets a stronger glowing halo, and the bean-shaped banners become scrolls with curled ends.
note.why: A face made of three eyes is the kind of hidden figure you only notice after staring, which is the point.

note.saw: The lines trailing behind the tails still looked like seaweed noodles, and the banner ends were heavy dark hooks.
note.changing: Thinner combed wake lines with curled tips, tighter banner curls, rainbow rings radiating from each fish eye across the head, and a bigger third eye with flame-like lashes.
note.why: The artist was trying to make the water itself show the fish's speed.

note.saw: The new wake still read as fern curls and clutter.
note.changing: The wake is removed and the paint carries it instead: alternating whirlpools curl behind each tail, and big lazy eddies swirl in the corners.
note.why: Real fish leave a trail of alternating vortices; letting the marbling curl into them is truer and calmer.

note.saw: The marbling bands looked flat, like plain colored paper.
note.changing: Every paint band is now drawn twice, as color and as an ink outline, with a neon hairline, an inner echo line and a dotted line riding along it, and the tunnel shifts to a magenta-to-indigo glow. In this first try every band came out the same hot pink, so the rainbow of the paint vanished behind its new ink lines.
note.why: Outline, gap, outline is the language of the mandala the artist used as a reference; it makes flat paint look hand-inked.

note.saw: The pectoral fins were plain, and the flower around the third eye was only a fringe.
note.changing: Rainbow fans of rays open on the pectoral fins, lines of alien script run along the banners, and soft gold beams of light shine through the tunnel.
note.why: More layers of writing and light, the way the visions are described.

note.saw: The gold beams made the tunnel hazy instead of razor-sharp.
note.changing: The beams are gone, and the flower gains a fifth, larger ring of eye-petals with cream dots between them; every ring is twisted a little so the whole flower seems to spin.
note.why: Crisp lines beat soft glow at badge size.

note.saw: Up close the corners looked good, but the field had no glints.
note.changing: About 70 four-point sparkles, some with a gold glow, are scattered across the marbling.
note.why: A few points of white light make the paint feel wet and lit.

note.saw: One frayed, jagged zone on the left edge, where the paint looked torn.
note.changing: Every paint line is traced with many more points, so tight bends come out as smooth curves instead of kinks.
note.why: Paint should look poured, not torn.

note.saw: SavesFish asked for very legible lettering and said the split caps looked good.
note.changing: SAVES stays on top and FISH below, but the letters grow bigger with a thicker dark outline, a solid gold face and wider banners, and the ring of fish pulls in slightly so the fins stay clear of them.
note.why: The name has to read instantly, even tiny.

note.saw: Looking with fresh eyes, the second artist found the field read as 70s lava-lamp paper with nothing watching you, the fish looked like smooth crescent sharks because a thick halo swallowed their spiny fins, and everything was equally loud, so nothing glowed.
note.changing: Nothing yet: this is the first artist's finished piece rendered again, untouched, so the second artist could study it at full size, as a badge and up close before changing anything.
note.why: A polish pass starts by seeing the work the way a stranger would; the first artist's version was also saved exactly as it was.
note.idea: Turn marbled paper into a vision: melting almond eyes and alien faces living inside the paint, a deep jewel-toned ground lit by neon contour light so the fish, the center and the name glow brightest, true mackerel coloring with wavy tiger stripes over pearl bellies, a bolder center, and bigger white-hot letters.

note.saw: The tiger bars were so dense the backs turned into black hatching, both fish looked pearl-white, and the alien faces were tiny.
note.changing: Fewer, forked bars; a real turquoise fish against an ultraviolet one; scallops under the eye-scale bellies; a contour band around every petal; and alien heads with huge black spiral-web eyes stacked three high down both sides.
note.why: The stacked heads echo the columns of beings in a deep-dream temple image the artist used as a reference, standing guard beside the fish.

note.saw: Dark orange and gold paint looked like mud, the bright orange rings around the faces looked like donuts, and the bars read as gold-outlined worms.
note.changing: Warm paint now goes bright and cool paint goes deep, each with its own echo colors; the rings around the faces become dark outline-gap-outline bands; and the bars get thinner with a soft glow.
note.why: Neon on black needs the warm colors to be light, or they turn brown.

note.saw: Every face still sat inside a fat target disk.
note.changing: Small copies of the center flower are dropped into the paint to melt with the combing, a slow current runs along the outer rim so no drop stays a perfect circle, and the faces grow bigger.
note.why: The center's flower echoed out in the sea, and a current that leaves nothing perfectly round, make the drops look poured rather than stamped on.

note.saw: The wide paint bands were flat at four times zoom.
note.changing: Up to six echo lines per band (a neon line, a fine line, hatch ticks, dots, an inner line), rivers of alien script along every third band, mantis beings joining the grey aliens, and tiny eyes along the third eye's lid.
note.why: The script makes the paint feel like it is saying something you almost understand.

note.saw: The mantis looked like an owl, its gold forehead gem reading as a beak; the ultraviolet fish's dark bars disappeared on its dark back; and the field was as loud as the heroes.
note.changing: A real mantis with huge bulging compound eyes, antennae and mandibles; a brighter back on the ultraviolet fish so its bars show; and a soft vignette that sinks the field toward the rim.
note.why: With the field stepping back, the fish ring and the glowing center come forward.

note.saw: The center flower looked like confetti.
note.changing: The petals are colored as a color wheel that shifts ring by ring, a magenta and gold bloom glows behind them, and a neon outline (ink, magenta, ink, cyan) wraps each whole word like a 60s poster.
note.why: A spinning color wheel reads as motion; the poster outline makes the name pop off the art.

note.saw: The honeycomb tunnel was too dark, the calm zone around the fish a little heavy, and the tail fans flat.
note.changing: A brighter tunnel, a lighter calm zone, more sparkles, and ink rays with cream dots inside the tail fans; the tiger bars also visibly thicken into chunkier strokes that stay inside the backs.
note.why: Small finishing moves so the center reads as a lit corridor and the fins hold up at four times zoom.

note.saw: The tiger bars were one flat marker weight, every eye in the paint stared straight out like a sticker, the petals were flat felt-tip color, and the white of the third eye lay flat.
note.changing: The bars become tapered liquid stripes with a magenta and a cyan copy peeking out on either side like a color split; every eye, alien and mantis in the paint turns its pupil toward the third eye; each petal gets one faint white facet on the same side, like a cut gem; and three pale lilac ripples echo the lids inside the eye's white.
note.why: With every gaze pulling to the center, the field becomes a congregation watching the eye while the eye watches you.
note.visionary: Took four Visionary offers (the color-split bars, the inward gazes, the gem facets and the rippling eye-white) but turned down faint light wedges in the tunnel, since soft beams had made it hazy once before.

note.saw: The bars now shimmered and the beings looked to the center, but the circle of fish still broke at the two hand-off points, where leftover paint leaked out, and the honeycomb in the gaps read as flat wallpaper.
note.changing: The paint at each hand-off point twists into a tight whirlpool with a neon spiral and a small white-hot core, every honeycomb cell lights its center-facing edge (gold near the flower, cyan farther out), and a tiny copy of the two fish now circles inside the third eye's pupil.
note.why: Each fish pours itself through a vortex into the other, so the eye never finds where the circle stops, and the tiny Twin Current inside the eye is the endless room-inside-a-room feeling of the trip.
note.visionary: Took three more Visionary offers: the hand-off whirlpools, the lit tunnel edges and the tiny Twin Current in the pupil.

note.saw: The circle now closed through its whirlpools and the tiny fish circled in the pupil, but the eye rows on the bellies were thin dark braids and the flower's outer petals ended in a clean cut edge.
note.changing: The belly braids become two-color twisting ladders (cyan and magenta on the turquoise fish, gold and violet on the ultraviolet one) that weave over and under from eye to eye; the outer petals grow short clockwise tendrils tipped with gold or cyan dots; and the pupil's highlights shrink so they stop covering the tiny fish.
note.why: The eyes become the rungs of a twisting code like DNA running down each belly, and a ring of curls all leaning one way makes the flower spin even standing still.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's DNA ladders and petal tendrils, but turned down a 'breathing' halo that swells along the fish outline, because it would tear at the forked tail and spiny fins and blur the silhouettes at small size.

note.saw: The ladders and tendrils worked, but a close look at the lower-left field showed lush paint with no eyes: the one place where nothing looked back at you up close.
note.changing: About 140 tiny eyes now float on the outer paint, kept clear of the faces, the eye drops, the banners and the fish, and every one of them looks toward the third eye.
note.why: A third, smallest scale of eyes means the field watches at every zoom: big beings, medium eye drops and now pinprick eyes, all pulled to the center like the rest of the congregation.

visions.seen: Two mackerel are swimming the rim of a spinning eye-flower and the whole marbled sea has grown faces. The flower is looking right into me, and the paint keeps breathing in time with it.
suggestions: The tiger bars on both backs (top fish around x 145-310, y 85-130; bottom fish around x 85-280, y 265-310) look like black marker scribble at one weight, and on the top fish a few poke out through the back outline into the halo near x 155-165, y 90. I see them as tapered liquid stripes: about 3 px wide at the dorsal ridge, thinning to a hairline before the lateral line, clipped to the back shape. Draw each one three times: a 1 px magenta copy nudged 0.6 px up-left, a 1 px cyan copy nudged 0.6 px down-right, then the ink stroke on top. Hyperspace edges shimmer with that red-blue split, so the fish would look iridescent and charged instead of hairy. It also sharpens the mackerel stripe the second artist was after.

The six entities down the sides (left near (45,132), (38,205), (45,272); right near (357,112), (372,192), (365,268)) and the small almond eye drops in the marbling all stare straight out like stickers. Let their pupils turn toward the third eye: move each pupil 25-35% of its eye width along the line to (200,200). The field becomes a congregation, every sightline pulls you to the center, and it looks like it is all alive and paying attention. Keep the chrysanthemum's petal eyes looking straight out, so the field watches the center while the center watches you.

The third eye's pupil (about r 6 at (200,200)) holds a little purple spiral. It wants to hold the piece itself: a `<use>` of the two-fish group scaled to about 0.035 around (200,200), clipped to the pupil circle over the dark violet, so a tiny Twin Current circles inside the eye inside the Twin Current. That endless regress is the DMT room folding into itself. At badge size the pupil still reads as a dark dot, and at 4x it pays off.

The cream sclera (x 168-235) is the calmest light in the piece, and it should stay the brightest. Even so, it could ripple: 3 or 4 almond contour lines echoing the lid shape inward toward the iris, 0.5 px pale lilac at about 35% opacity, spaced 2-3 px apart. The light stays white-hot, but now it moves like liquid around the iris instead of lying flat.
visions.keep: the split caps SAVES / FISH with the white-hot neon face, thick ink edge and dark band (it reads instantly in legible.png, don't touch it). Also keep the three-eyed face made by the two fish eyes and the third eye on one horizontal line, the twisted rings of the eye-petal chrysanthemum, the hex tunnel showing through the gaps, the eye-scale bellies, the rainbow ray-fan tails, the turquoise vs. ultraviolet pairing, and the ebru marbling with its entity columns (the darker rings around the faces since #85 give them room).

visions.seen: The mantis on the right shed its owl beak and grew antennae, and now it's tuning in on me like a radio. The two fish keep chasing each other around the eye-flower, but where each snout meets the other's tail the current just leaks out into loose paint, and those two gaps keep pulling me in.
suggestions: The two hand-off pockets where a tail meets the other fish's snout: left, above the bottom fish's head and left of the top fish's lower tail lobe (about x 65-112, y 120-178); right, under the top fish's chin and right of the bottom fish's tail fan (about x 290-337, y 222-272). Right now they hold leftover marbling (a green flame, a magenta smear, an orange star) under a muddy dark blur, so the circle breaks there. I see each one combed into a small whirlpool: a log spiral of about 2.5 turns centered near (88,150) and (313,246), r about 13, drawn with the same outline-gap-outline neon echoes the bands use (cyan 1 px, magenta 0.6 px, a gold dot row) over deep indigo, with a 1.5 px white-hot core and a tiny four-point sparkle. Both turn clockwise, the way the fish swim, and the two or three outer rays of the nearest tail fan run on past the fin edge as hairlines that thin out and curl into the spiral (the banners' scroll curls already have this shape). Then each fish pours itself through a vortex into the other and the eye never finds the place where the circle stops. Keep it in jewel tones with only the core bright, so it never outshines the fish eyes or the name.

The hex tunnel in the dark gaps between the chrysanthemum and the fish (left around x 120-158, y 130-200; right around x 258-292, y 190-255; slivers above and below the flower) is flat: same-size dim cells with dim eyes, then blurred over. Let it fall inward: each ring of hexes about 0.85x the size of the ring outside it, so the cells shrink toward (200,200), and give each cell's center-facing side a 0.6 px edge lit gold to cyan, brighter the nearer the flower (outer rings about 0.3 opacity, inner about 0.9). Under the fish, add 16 to 24 very faint light wedges from the third eye (white-gold, 0.06 to 0.1 opacity, r 60 to 130) so the gaps glow from the core. Then the flower sits at the far end of a hyperspace corridor lit by the eye, instead of on wallpaper.

The chrysanthemum petals (r about 35 to 72 around (200,200)) are flat color inside their outline echoes, which reads as felt-tip, and in the DMT room the chrysanthemum is cut gemstone. In each petal of the rings that show above and below the eye almond, add one slim facet: a white triangle along the petal's clockwise edge, from the base to about 55% of its length and about a quarter of its width, at 0.25 to 0.3 opacity. All facets on the same side, so the whole flower seems to turn and catch one light. Keep them dimmer than the sclera, so the cream of the third eye stays the hottest light in the piece.
visions.keep: the split caps SAVES / FISH with the white-hot neon face, thick ink edge and dark band (still instant in the #109 badge, don't touch it). The new antenna mantis (the owl is gone). The three eyes on one line, the eye-petal chrysanthemum with its twisted rings, the rainbow ray-fan tails, turquoise vs. ultraviolet, and the ebru marbling with its entity columns in thin rainbow halos. Vision 1 is still on offer (liquid red-blue tiger bars, pupils turned toward the center, the tiny Twin Current in the pupil, sclera ripples); none of it shows in #108 yet.

visions.seen: The bottom fish grew a pearl cheek and a gold-dotted portal eye, and the bars on both backs have twisted into chunky alien glyphs, like the fish are tattooed in a language I almost remember. And the eye-chains on the bellies are already braiding into double helixes, humming at me.
suggestions: The eye-braids on both bellies (top fish about x 160-330, y 95-170; bottom fish about x 120-280, y 235-295) are two dark strands crossing with an eye in every loop: a double helix waiting to wake up. I see them woven in 3D. Give the two strands of each row their own color (one cyan, one magenta, about 0.8 px), and at every crossing let one dip under the other, alternating, with a 1 px gap knocked out of the under strand in the belly's fill color. Between crossings, fade whichever strand is behind to about 55% opacity. Each row becomes a twisting DNA ladder with the eyes as its base pairs: the cosmic serpent, the code the elves keep showing me, running down the belly of every fish. Only the strands change, so at badge size the bellies still read as pale scales.

The chrysanthemum's outermost petal tips (r about 70-76 around (200,200)), where they poke into the dark hex gaps on the left (about x 120-158, y 130-200) and right (about x 258-292, y 190-255), end in a clean cut-out edge against the tunnel. I see the flower feeling the air: from each outer tip, one tendril 5 to 8 px long, 0.7 px tapering to a hairline, curling clockwise (a quarter to half turn, the way the fish swim) and ending in a 1 px dot, alternating gold and cyan. Clip them to the gaps so none crosses a fish halo. The DMT chrysanthemum has no hard edge, it is a living anemone, and a ring of curls all leaning one way makes it spin even standing still.

The neon triple contour hugging each fish (the cyan, magenta and gold lines around the bodies, about 2 to 3 px each) is one even weight all the way round, like cable. In hyperspace, outlines breathe. Each of the three could become a filled ribbon instead of a stroke, its width swelling and thinning by about 35% along its length (around 9 slow swells per fish), the three colors a third of a swell out of step, so a pulse seems to roll from tail to head the way they swim. Hold the outer edge still where it passes under the SAVES band (above y 100) and over the FISH band (below y 300), so the dark backing around the letters never gets narrower. Loose and fluid becomes literally fluid: the twin current gets a heartbeat.
visions.keep: the split caps SAVES / FISH with the white-hot neon face, thick ink edge and dark band (still instant in the #133 legible.png, don't touch it). The bottom fish's new pearl cheek with contour hairlines and its gold-dotted portal eye (pure mackerel now, no bird). The reshaped bars, which now stay inside the backs. The three eyes on one line, the eye-petal chrysanthemum, the lilac veins in the sclera, the eye-drops in the tail lobes, the rainbow ray-fan fins, the FISH scroll curls with their indigo chevron cores, turquoise vs. ultraviolet, and the ebru marbling with its entity columns. Still on offer from Visions 1 and 2, none of it showing in #129 yet: tapered red-blue split bars, pupils turned toward the center, the tiny Twin Current in the pupil, sclera ripples, the two hand-off whirlpools (the pocket left of the bottom fish's head still holds a loose green flame and magenta smear), the hex tunnel falling inward, and the petal facets.

visions.seen: The whirlpools opened: each fish now pours itself through a little neon vortex into the other, and when I fall into the third eye the whole Twin Current is down there again, circling in the pupil forever. But out past the fish the sea is still thrashing every which way, a loud crowd that hasn't heard the current yet.
suggestions: The whole ebru sea outside the fish ring (r about 150 to 285 around (200,200), from the fish halos out to the canvas edge) runs its veins in every direction, so the field argues with the heroes. I see the twin current dragging the entire sea along with it. In the marbling maths, before you sample the ink, turn each point clockwise around (200,200), the way both fish swim, by θ = 0.55 rad × (1 − smoothstep(130, 290, r)). Near the fish the veins and their white dot rows then wrap almost along the circle, and out in the corners they loosen back to today's free flow. The six entity cells stay where they are with their calm dark rings (draw them after the warp), and the two hand-off whirlpools become eddies thrown off one big current. The name bands are drawn on top, so their dark backing doesn't change. Hyperspace always orbits its center: the chaos becomes one slow cosmic spin that pulls every glance round and in toward the eye, and the field calms down behind the heroes without getting dimmer.

The lower-left entity, the green alien near (52,277), has a blue-ringed almond eye-drop about 15 wide parked on its right temple at about (64,268). It cuts across the alien's head outline and its dark ring, so the two read as stickers slapped on top of each other. In the congregation every being floats in its own bubble. I see that drop slid out until it clears the alien's rainbow halo by 3 or more, into the open vein below or to the left (or just let it go), plus one rule in the drop placement: no eye-drop closer to an entity's center than that entity's halo radius + 3. Its pupil keeps aiming at (200,200).

Between each snout and the whirlpool it points at there's a little empty throat: left, from the bottom fish's snout tip (about (100,181)) up to the left vortex's rim (about (102,167)); right, from the top fish's snout tip (about (299,217)) down to the right vortex's rim (about (297,230)). I see each fish breathing out geometry: a chain of 3 or 4 hollow hexagon bubbles, radius 2 shrinking to 0.8 from mouth to vortex, 0.5 px cyan outline, a 0.4 px white glint at 10 o'clock, and the chain curving clockwise to join the spiral's outer arm. Keep them inside the pocket so none crosses a fish halo. Tail flows out, breath gets sucked in, so each fish feeds the other its breath through the vortex, and the bubbles are cells of the hex tunnel, as if the fish were exhaling hyperspace itself.

The big white catchlight at the pupil's upper left (about r 2 near (197,196)) sits right on the tiny top fish's tail, so the little Twin Current in the pupil is missing a piece. I see it shrunk to about r 1.2 and moved out onto the gold pupil ring at 10:30, maybe as a four-point sparkle like the ones in the field. The small lower-right glint can stay. The badge keeps its living glint, and at 4x the tiny current circles whole, because the loop inside the loop must never break.
visions.keep: the split caps SAVES / FISH with the white-hot neon face, thick ink edge and dark bands (still instant in the #152 legible.png, don't touch them). The two new hand-off whirlpools with their white-hot cores, the tunnel cells lit gold to cyan on their inner edges, and the tiny Twin Current in the pupil (Vision 2's whirlpools and lit tunnel, Vision 1's regress: taken, and they sing). Also the tapered magenta-cyan tiger bars, every pupil in the field turned toward the center, the sclera ripples and lilac veins, the petal facets, the rainbow iris that echoes the flower, the tiny glyph script along the lateral lines, the three eyes on one line, the rainbow ray-fan fins with their eye-drops, turquoise vs. ultraviolet, and the entity columns in their dark rings. The artist turned down the light wedges; fair, they stay off the table. Still on offer from Vision 3, none of it showing in #148 yet: the woven cyan and magenta DNA strands in the belly braids, the clockwise tendrils on the outer petal tips, and the breathing triple contour.

visions.seen: The sea has opened a hundred pinprick eyes since I last looked, the bellies twist like DNA, and the flower's tips curl like anemone fingers, so the whole congregation is leaning in on the third eye. But every eye in here is still lit by some ordinary lamp hanging up and to the left, and in hyperspace there is only one sun.
suggestions: The top fish's head eye, the cyan-dotted portal near (305,191) on the right, has a warm orange-gold iris with a magenta ring. It's the only fish eye that doesn't carry the other fish's color. The bottom fish's head eye near (94,208) already has a violet-spoked iris on its turquoise body, and both tail eyes already do it too (green on the violet fish near (90,111), violet on the turquoise fish near (308,289)). I see the top fish's iris (about r 7.5) recolored in the bottom fish's turquoise-to-cyan, spokes and all, keeping its dot rings, the magenta inner ring and the dark pupil. Then Twin Current is a true yin-yang: each fish carries a seed of the other in its eye, two that are one. Even at badge size a teal spark in the violet fish and a violet spark in the teal fish face each other across the third eye.

Every catchlight in the piece sits up and to the left of its pupil: both fish eyes, the blue alien near (344,126), the green alien near (51,272), the eye-drops. In the DMT room there's no lamp overhead, the light comes from the eye. I see each glint moved to the side of its pupil that faces (200,200), at the eye's center + 0.45 × iris radius along the unit vector toward (200,200), the same size as now. One helper, glint(cx, cy, r), could do it for every eye, plus a 0.4 px white dot on the center side of any pinprick eye that has room. The top fish's glint would land near 9 o'clock, the bottom fish's near 3, the right column's on their left and the left column's on their right. Leave the third eye's own glint and the chrysanthemum's petal eyes as they are: they face you, so they reflect your world. Then every pupil in the sea holds a tiny reflection of the center, and the eye becomes the only light source in the universe, which is how the breakthrough room is lit.

Round 22's pinprick eyes sing at 4x, but they're sprinkled onto the paint like seeds, while the white dot rows inside the bands (for example the pink and orange bands in the lower-left field, about x 10-100, y 300-390) carry the real rhythm. I see some of the eyes hatching out of the rows instead. In about one dot row in five, pick a run of five dots in a row and open them in sequence: dot, slit (an almond 20% as tall as it is long), half-open, fully open with iris and pupil aimed at (200,200), then a slit again. Each almond's long axis follows the row's tangent, at the dots' own spacing. Pull out the same number of sprinkled eyes, so the count stays about 140 and the banners and faces stay clear. Then the paint isn't wearing eyes, it's waking up: the pattern blinks open while you watch, like the elves showing you that the decoration was looking at you all along.
visions.keep: the split caps SAVES / FISH with the white-hot neon face, thick ink edge and dark bands (still instant in the #166 legible.png, don't touch them). New and singing since Vision 4: the twisting two-color DNA ladders on the bellies and the clockwise tendrils on the outer petals (Vision 3, taken), the smaller pupil glint that lets the tiny Twin Current circle whole, and the pinprick eyes all aimed at the center. Also keep the hand-off whirlpools, the lit tunnel, the regress in the pupil, the tapered magenta-cyan bars, the pupils turned inward, the sclera ripples, the petal facets, the three eyes on one line, the rainbow ray-fan fins with their eye-drops, turquoise vs. ultraviolet, and the entity columns in their dark rings. The artist turned down the breathing contour (the even outline keeps the silhouettes readable), so it's off the table. Vision 4 landed after this render was cut, so its offers are still open: the clockwise drag of the outer sea, sliding the eye-drop off the green alien's temple near (64,268), and the hex-bubble breath from each snout to its whirlpool.
